Mixue Ice Cream & Tea.text: It began in 1997 as a shaved-ice stall in Zhengzhou, paid for with a CN¥3,000 loan from the founder's grandmother.
Mixue Ice Cream & Tea.evidence: In June 1997, Zhang Hongchao was studying at Henan University of Economics and Law when he opened a shaved‑ice stall in Zhengzhou using a CN¥3,000 loan from his grandmother.

McDonald's.text: Its first mascot was Speedee, a chef with a hamburger for a head; Ronald McDonald only arrived in 1963.
McDonald's.evidence: The original mascot of McDonald's was a hamburger-headed chef who was referred to as "Speedee". In 1962, the Golden Arches replaced Speedee as the universal mascot. Clown mascot Ronald McDonald was introduced in 1963 to market the chain to children.

Starbucks.text: The founders hunted for a name starting with "st" and landed on Starbuck, the chief mate in Moby-Dick.
Starbucks.evidence: Terry Heckler, thought words beginning with the letters "st" were powerful, leading the founders to create a list of words beginning with "st", hoping to find a brand name. ... From there, the group remembered "Starbuck", the name of the chief mate in the book Moby-Dick.

Luckin Coffee.text: Delisted in 2020 after its COO faked about US$310 million of sales, it bounced back as China's largest coffee chain.
Luckin Coffee.evidence: On 2 April 2020, however, the company announced that an internal investigation found that its chief operating officer, Jian Liu, had fabricated the company's 2019 sales by "around RMB2.2 billion" (US$310 million). ... the company was delisted from NASDAQ on 29 June 2020. ... expanding to more than 36,000 stores to become China's largest coffee chain

Subway.text: Its parent company is Doctor's Associates: the founder hoped the shop would pay his way through medical school.
Subway.evidence: In 1965, Fred DeLuca borrowed $1,000 from his friend Peter Buck ... they formed Doctor's Associates Inc. to oversee operations of the restaurants as the franchise expanded. The holding company derives its name from DeLuca's goal to earn enough from the business to pay tuition for medical school, as well as Buck's having a doctorate in physics.

KFC.text: The name Kentucky Fried Chicken was coined by a sign painter working for its first franchisee, in Utah.
KFC.evidence: In 1952, Sanders franchised his recipe to his friend Pete Harman of South Salt Lake, Utah ... Don Anderson, a sign painter hired by Harman, coined the name "Kentucky Fried Chicken".

Domino's.text: Co-founder Jim Monaghan traded his half of the business to his brother for the VW Beetle they used for deliveries.
Domino's.evidence: Within eight months, Jim traded his half of the business to Tom for the Volkswagen Beetle they used for pizza deliveries.

Wallace.text: It started out copying KFC and McDonald's, then took off with 1 yuan Cokes, 2 yuan chicken thighs and 3 yuan burgers.
Wallace.evidence: Initially, they mimicked the menu and prices of Western giants KFC and McDonald's, but customers preferred the original establishments. The brothers then launched a "Special 1-2-3 Price" promotion (1 yuan for a Coke, 2 yuan for chicken thighs, and 3 yuan for a hamburger), which doubled their sales.

Pizza Hut.text: In 2001 it delivered a vacuum-sealed pizza to the International Space Station, where Yuri Usachov ate it in orbit.
Pizza Hut.evidence: Pizza Hut developed a pizza to be delivered to the International Space Station in 2001. It was vacuum-sealed and about 6 in (15 cm) in diameter to fit in the station's oven. It was launched on a Soyuz and eaten by Yuri Usachov in orbit.

Burger King.text: In Australia it's Hungry Jack's, because a takeaway shop in Adelaide already owned the Burger King name.
Burger King.evidence: Australia is the only country in which Burger King does not operate under its own name. When the company set about establishing operations down under in 1971, it found that its business name was already trademarked by a takeaway food shop in Adelaide.
